The cell corpse (or its fragments) may be engulfed by an adjacent cell in vivo, but engulfment of whole cells should not be considered a strict criteria to define cell death as, under some circumstances, live engulfed cells can be released from phagosomes (see PMID:18045538).

entities.selected_description: A pearson correlation coefficient calculation is a similarity calculation which attaches to each pair of random variables X and Y the ratio of their covariance by the product of their standard deviations. Given a series of n measurements of X and Y written as x_i and y_i where i = 1, 2, ..., n, then their Pearson correlation coefficient refers to the "sample correlation coefficient" and is written as the sum over i of the ratios (x_i-xbar)*(y_i-ybar)/((n-1)*s_x*s_y) where xbar and ybar are the sample means of X and Y , s_x and s_y are the sample standard deviations of X and Y. The closer the pearson correlation coefficient is to 1, the more similar the inputs are considered.

entities.label: photorespiratory metabolism
entities.selected_description: A light-dependent catabolic process occurring concomitantly with photosynthesis in plants (especially C3 plants) whereby dioxygen (O2) is consumed and carbon dioxide (CO2) is evolved. The substrate is glycolate formed in large quantities in chloroplasts from 2-phosphoglycolate generated from ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate by the action of ribulose-bisphosphate carboxylase; the glycolate enters the peroxisomes where it is converted by glycolate oxidase to glyoxylate which undergoes transamination to glycine. This then passes into the mitochondria where it is decarboxylated forming one molecule of serine for every two molecules of glycine. This pathway also exists in photosynthetic bacteria.

entities.selected_label: biological process involved in symbiotic interaction
entities.selected_description: A process carried out by gene products in an organism that enable the organism to engage in a symbiotic relationship, a more or less intimate association, with another organism. The various forms of symbiosis include parasitism, in which the association is disadvantageous or destructive to one of the organisms; mutualism, in which the association is advantageous, or often necessary to one or both and not harmful to either; and commensalism, in which one member of the association benefits while the other is not affected. However, mutualism, parasitism, and commensalism are often not discrete categories of interactions and should rather be perceived as a continuum of interaction ranging from parasitism to mutualism. In fact, the direction of a symbiotic interaction can change during the lifetime of the symbionts due to developmental changes as well as changes in the biotic/abiotic environment in which the interaction occurs. Microscopic symbionts are often referred to as endosymbionts.

entities.label: ribosome
entities.selected_description: An intracellular organelle, about 200 A in diameter, consisting of RNA and protein. It is the site of protein biosynthesis resulting from translation of messenger RNA (mRNA). It consists of two subunits, one large and one small, each containing only protein and RNA. Both the ribosome and its subunits are characterized by their sedimentation coefficients, expressed in Svedberg units (symbol: S). Hence, the prokaryotic ribosome (70S) comprises a large (50S) subunit and a small (30S) subunit, while the eukaryotic ribosome (80S) comprises a large (60S) subunit and a small (40S) subunit. Two sites on the ribosomal large subunit are involved in translation, namely the aminoacyl site (A site) and peptidyl site (P site). Ribosomes from prokaryotes, eukaryotes, mitochondria, and chloroplasts have characteristically distinct ribosomal proteins.

entities.label: spliceosome
entities.selected_description: Any of a series of ribonucleoprotein complexes that contain snRNA(s) and small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs), and are formed sequentially during the spliceosomal splicing of one or more substrate RNAs, and which also contain the RNA substrate(s) from the initial target RNAs of splicing, the splicing intermediate RNA(s), to the final RNA products. During cis-splicing, the initial target RNA is a single, contiguous RNA transcript, whether mRNA, snoRNA, etc., and the released products are a spliced RNA and an excised intron, generally as a lariat structure. During trans-splicing, there are two initial substrate RNAs, the spliced leader RNA and a pre-mRNA.

concepts.label: piperonylic acid
concepts.description: A member of the class of benzodioxoles that is 1,3-benzodioxole substituted by a carboxy group at position 5. It is a natural product isolated from several plant species. It is a selective mechanism-based inactivator of the trans-cinnamate 4-hydroxylase enzyme and exhibits antifungal and skin wound healing properties.

concepts.label: fatty acid 18:3
concepts.description: Any trienoic fatty acid containing 18 carbons.

concepts.label: (15)N-modified compound
concepts.description: An isotopically modified compound in which the abundance of a <small><sup>15</small></sup>N isotope at one or more positions has been increased above that of the naturally occurring level.

concepts.label: ATP
concepts.description: An adenosine 5'-phosphate in which the 5'-phosphate is a triphosphate group. It is involved in the transportation of chemical energy during metabolic pathways.

concepts.label: glycine
concepts.description: The simplest (and the only achiral) proteinogenic amino acid, with a hydrogen atom as its side chain.

concepts.label: hexadecanoic acid
concepts.description: A straight-chain, sixteen-carbon, saturated long-chain fatty acid.

concepts.label: long-chain fatty acid
concepts.description: A fatty acid with a chain length ranging from C<small><sub>13</sub></small> to C<small><sub>22</sub></small>.

concepts.label: dihydroxyacetone
concepts.description: A ketotriose consisting of acetone bearing hydroxy substituents at positions 1 and 3. The simplest member of the class of ketoses and the parent of the class of glycerones.

concepts.label: dihydroxyacetone phosphate
concepts.description: A member of the class of glycerone phosphates that consists of glycerone bearing a single phospho substituent.

concepts.label: oleic acid
concepts.description: An octadec-9-enoic acid in which the double bond at C-9 has Z (cis) stereochemistry.

concepts.label: hydrogen peroxide
concepts.description: An inorganic peroxide consisting of two hydroxy groups joined by a covalent oxygen-oxygen single bond.

concepts.label: phospholipid
concepts.description: A lipid containing phosphoric acid as a mono- or di-ester. The term encompasses phosphatidic acids and phosphoglycerides.

concepts.label: lipopolysaccharide
concepts.description: Liposaccharide natural compounds consisting of a trisaccharide repeating unit (two heptose units and octulosonic acid) with oligosaccharide side chains and 3-hydroxytetradecanoic acid units (they are a major constituent of the cell walls of Gram-negative bacteria).

concepts.label: L-valine
concepts.description: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of valine.

concepts.label: L-arginine
concepts.description: An <small>L</small>-α-amino acid that is the <small>L</small>-isomer of arginine.

concepts.label: NADPH
concepts.description: The reduced form of NADP+; used in anabolic reactions, such as lipid and nucleic acid synthesis, which require NADPH as a reducing agent.

concepts.label: carbon dioxide
concepts.description: A one-carbon compound with formula CO<small><sub>2</sub></small> in which the carbon is attached to each oxygen atom by a double bond. A colourless, odourless gas under normal conditions, it is produced during respiration by all animals, fungi and microorganisms that depend directly or indirectly on living or decaying plants for food.

concepts.label: L-methionine
concepts.description: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of methionine.

concepts.label: carbohydrate
concepts.description: Any member of the class of organooxygen compounds that is a polyhydroxy-aldehyde or -ketone or a lactol resulting from their intramolecular condensation (monosaccharides); substances derived from these by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditols), by oxidation of one or more hydroxy groups to afford the corresponding aldehydes, ketones, or carboxylic acids, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by a hydrogen atom; and polymeric products arising by intermolecular acetal formation between two or more such molecules (disaccharides, polysaccharides and oligosaccharides). Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms; prior to any oxidation or reduction, most have the empirical formula Cm(H2O)n. Compounds obtained from carbohydrates by substitution, etc., are known as carbohydrate derivatives and may contain other elements. Cyclitols are generally not regarded as carbohydrates.

concepts.label: acyl sugars
concepts.description: Any saccharolipid having one or more sugars bound to fatty acyl chain(s).

concepts.label: 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositol
concepts.description: A phosphatidylinositol in which the inositol moiety is the 1D-myo isomer and the phosphatidyl group is located at its position 1.

concepts.label: L-tryptophan
concepts.description: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of tryptophan.

concepts.label: glutathione
concepts.description: A tripeptide compound consisting of glutamic acid attached via its side chain to the N-terminus of cysteinylglycine.

concepts.label: gamma-aminobutyric acid
concepts.description: A γ-amino acid that is butanoic acid with the amino substituent located at C-4.

concepts.label: D-mannitol
concepts.description: The <small>D</small>-enantiomer of mannitol.

concepts.label: salicylic acid
concepts.description: A monohydroxybenzoic acid that is benzoic acid with a hydroxy group at the ortho position. It is obtained from the bark of the white willow and wintergreen leaves.

concepts.label: glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
concepts.description: An aldotriose phosphate that is the 3-phospho derivative of glyceraldehyde. It is an important metabolic intermediate in several central metabolic pathways in all organisms.

concepts.label: L-proline
concepts.description: Pyrrolidine in which the pro-S hydrogen at position 2 is substituted by a carboxylic acid group. L-Proline is the only one of the twenty DNA-encoded amino acids which has a secondary amino group α to the carboxyl group. It is an essential component of collagen and is important for proper functioning of joints and tendons. It also helps maintain and strengthen heart muscles.

concepts.label: linoleic acid
concepts.description: An octadecadienoic acid in which the two double bonds are at positions 9 and 12 and have Z (cis) stereochemistry.

concepts.label: 1,2-diacyl-3-beta-D-galactosyl-sn-glycerol
concepts.description: A class of galactoglycerolipids that consists of any 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol having a β-D-galactosyl residue attached at position 3.

concepts.label: nitrate
concepts.description: A nitrogen oxoanion formed by loss of a proton from nitric acid. Principal species present at pH 7.3.

concepts.label: glycine betaine
concepts.description: The amino acid betaine derived from glycine.

concepts.label: plastoquinone
concepts.description: A polyprenylbenzoquinone that is 2,3-dimethylbenzoquinone with a polyprenyl side chain at position 5. There are several naturally-occurring plastoquinones with side chains of different length (containing between 6 and 9 isoprene units).

concepts.label: acyl-CoA
concepts.description: A thioester that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of any carboxylic acid.

concepts.label: sucrose
concepts.description: A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.

concepts.label: dinitrogen
concepts.description: An elemental molecule consisting of two trivalently-bonded nitrogen atoms.

concepts.label: L-glutamine
concepts.description: An optically active form of glutamine having <small>L</small>-configuration.

concepts.label: lipid
concepts.description: 'Lipids' is a loosely defined term for substances of biological origin that are soluble in nonpolar solvents. They consist of saponifiable lipids, such as glycerides (fats and oils) and phospholipids, as well as nonsaponifiable lipids, principally steroids.

concepts.label: glutamic acid
concepts.description: An α-amino acid that is glutaric acid bearing a single amino substituent at position 2.

concepts.label: 4-hydroxy-L-proline
concepts.description: The <small>L</small>-stereoisomer of 4-hydroxyproline.

concepts.label: CaMn4O5 cluster
concepts.description: A metal-oxygen cluster containing 1 calcium atom, 4 managanese atoms and 5 oxygen atoms. It is the catalytic center of water oxidation in photosystem II (PSII).

concepts.label: alkaloid
concepts.description: Any of the naturally occurring, basic nitrogen compounds (mostly heterocyclic) occurring mostly in the plant kingdom, but also found in bacteria, fungi, and animals. By extension, certain neutral compounds biogenetically related to basic alkaloids are also classed as alkaloids. Amino acids, peptides, proteins, nucleotides, nucleic acids, amino sugars and antibiotics are not normally regarded as alkaloids. Compounds in which the nitrogen is exocyclic (dopamine, mescaline, serotonin, etc.) are usually classed as amines rather than alkaloids.

concepts.label: all-cis-7,10,13-hexadecatrienoic acid
concepts.description: A hexadecatrienoic acid having Z double bonds at positions 7, 10 and 13.

concepts.label: asparagine
concepts.description: An α-amino acid in which one of the hydrogens attached to the α-carbon of glycine is substituted by a 2-amino-2-oxoethyl group.

concepts.label: cinnamate
concepts.description: A member of the class of cinnamates that results from the deprotonation of the carboxy group of cinnamic acid.

concepts.label: coumarate
concepts.description: A member of the class of cinnamates obtained by the deprotonation of the carboxy group of coumaric acid.

concepts.label: coumaric acid
concepts.description: A monohydroxycinnamic acid that is prop-2-enoic acid substituted by a hydroxyphenyl group at position 3.

concepts.label: (+)-abscisic acid
concepts.description: The naturally occurring (1'S)-(+) enantiomer of abscisic acid. It is an important sesquiterpenoid plant hormone which acts as a regulator of plant responses to environmental stresses such as drought and cold.

concepts.label: hormone
concepts.description: Originally referring to an endogenous compound that is formed in specialized organ or group of cells and carried to another organ or group of cells, in the same organism, upon which it has a specific regulatory function, the term is now commonly used to include non-endogenous, semi-synthetic and fully synthetic analogues of such compounds.

concepts.label: insecticide
concepts.description: Strictly, a substance intended to kill members of the class Insecta. In common usage, any substance used for preventing, destroying, repelling or controlling insects.

concepts.label: linolenic acid
concepts.description: A two-membered subclass of octadecatrienoic acid comprising the (9Z,12Z,15Z)- and (6Z,9Z,12Z)-isomers. Linolenic acids are nutrients essential to the formation of prostaglandins and are also used in making paints and synthetic resins.

concepts.label: metabolite
concepts.description: Any intermediate or product resulting from metabolism. The term 'metabolite' subsumes the classes commonly known as primary and secondary metabolites.

concepts.label: octadecadienoic acid
concepts.description: Any straight-chain, C<small><sub>18</sub></small> polyunsaturated fatty acid having two C=C double bonds.

concepts.label: octadecatrienoic acid
concepts.description: Any trienoic fatty acid having eighteen carbons.

concepts.label: osmolyte
concepts.description: A solute used by a cell under water stress to maintain cell volume.

concepts.label: phenylpropanoid
concepts.description: Any organic aromatic compound with a structure based on a phenylpropane skeleton. The class includes naturally occurring phenylpropanoid esters, flavonoids, anthocyanins, coumarins and many small phenolic molecules as well as their semi-synthetic and synthetic analogues. Phenylpropanoids are also precursors of lignin.

concepts.label: polyphenol
concepts.description: Members of the class of phenols that contain 2 or more benzene rings each of which is substituted by at least one hydroxy group.

concepts.label: polyunsaturated fatty acid
concepts.description: Any fatty acid containing more than one double bond. Acids in this group are reported to have cardioprotective effects; and levels are lowered in chronic fatigue syndrome.

concepts.label: reactive oxygen species
concepts.description: Molecules or ions formed by the incomplete one-electron reduction of oxygen. They contribute to the microbicidal activity of phagocytes, regulation of signal transduction and gene expression, and the oxidative damage to biopolymers.

concepts.label: saturated fatty acid
concepts.description: Any fatty acid containing no carbon to carbon multiple bonds. Known to produce adverse biological effects when ingested to excess.

concepts.label: unsaturated fatty acid
concepts.description: Any fatty acid containing at least one C=C or C≡C bond.

concepts.label: cinnamic acid
concepts.description: A monocarboxylic acid that consists of acrylic acid bearing a phenyl substituent at the 3-position. It is found in Cinnamomum cassia.

concepts.label: dimethyl sulfoxide
concepts.description: A 2-carbon sulfoxide in which the sulfur atom has two methyl substituents.

concepts.label: glutamine
concepts.description: An α-amino acid that consists of butyric acid bearing an amino substituent at position 2 and a carbamoyl substituent at position 4.

concepts.label: all-cis-5,8,11,14,17-icosapentaenoic acid
concepts.description: An icosapentaenoic acid having five cis-double bonds at positions 5, 8, 11, 14 and 17.

concepts.label: 3-[alpha-D-galactosyl-(1->6)-beta-D-galactosyl]-1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol
concepts.description: A digalactosylglycerol derivative in which the digalactosyl moiety is α-<small>D</small>-galactosyl-(1→6)-β-<small>D</small>-galactosyl at O-3, with O-1 and O-2 both acylated.

concepts.label: palmitoleic acid
concepts.description: A hexadec-9-enoic acid in which the double bond at position C-9 has cis configuration.

concepts.label: erucic acid
concepts.description: A docosenoic acid having a cis- double bond at C-13. It is found particularly in brassicas - it is a major component of mustard and rapeseed oils and is produced by broccoli, Brussels sprouts, kale, and wallflowers.

concepts.label: octadecanoic acid
concepts.description: A C<small><sub>18</sub></small> straight-chain saturated fatty acid component of many animal and vegetable lipids. As well as in the diet, it is used in hardening soaps, softening plastics and in making cosmetics, candles and plastics.

concepts.label: ammonium
concepts.description: An onium cation obtained by protonation of ammonia.

concepts.label: chlorophyll
concepts.description: A family of magnesium porphyrins, defined by the presence of a fifth ring beyond the four pyrrole-like rings. The rings can have various side chains which usually include a long phytol chain.

concepts.label: glycolate
concepts.description: A hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion that is acetate where the methyl group has been hydroxylated.

concepts.label: decanoic acid
concepts.description: A C<small><sub>10</sub></small>, straight-chain saturated fatty acid.

concepts.label: 1,2-diacyl-3-(alpha-D-6-sulfoquinovosyl)-sn-glycerol
concepts.description: A glycosylglycerol derivative in which the glycosyl moiety is α-<small>D</small>-6-sulfoquinovosyl attached at O-3, with O-1 and O-2 both acylated.

concepts.label: 4-coumarate
concepts.description: A coumarate that is the conjugate base of 4-coumaric acid.

concepts.label: nucleic acid
concepts.description: A macromolecule made up of nucleotide units and hydrolysable into certain pyrimidine or purine bases (usually adenine, cytosine, guanine, thymine, uracil), <small>D</small>-ribose or 2-deoxy-<small>D</small>-ribose and phosphoric acid.

concepts.label: ribonucleic acid
concepts.description: High molecular weight, linear polymers, composed of nucleotides containing ribose and linked by phosphodiester bonds; RNA is central to the synthesis of proteins.

concepts.label: amino acid
concepts.description: A carboxylic acid containing one or more amino groups.

concepts.label: fatty acid
concepts.description: Any aliphatic monocarboxylic acid derived from or contained in esterified form in an animal or vegetable fat, oil or wax. Natural fatty acids commonly have a chain of 4 to 28 carbons (usually unbranched and even-numbered), which may be saturated or unsaturated. By extension, the term is sometimes used to embrace all acyclic aliphatic carboxylic acids.

concepts.label: docosenoic acid
concepts.description: A C<small><sub>22</sub></small>, monounsaturated fatty acid carrying a C=C double bond at any position.

concepts.label: protein
concepts.description: A biological macromolecule minimally consisting of one polypeptide chain synthesized at the ribosome.

concepts.label: 4-coumaric acid
concepts.description: A coumaric acid in which the hydroxy substituent is located at C-4 of the phenyl ring.

concepts.label: glyoxylate
concepts.description: The conjugate base of glyoxylic acid.

concepts.label: nitrogen-15 atom
concepts.description: The stable isotope of nitrogen with relative atomic mass 15.000109. The least abundant (0.368 atom percent) isotope of naturally occurring nitrogen.

concepts.label: (1->3)-beta-D-glucan
concepts.description: A β-<small>D</small>-glucan in which the glucose units are connected by (1→3) linkages.

concepts.label: bacteriochlorophyll
concepts.description: Chlorophylls of photosynthetic bacteria.

concepts.label: pentadecanoic acid
concepts.description: A straight-chain saturated fatty acid containing fifteen-carbon atoms.

concepts.label: malonaldehyde
concepts.description: A dialdehyde that is propane substituted by two oxo groups at the terminal carbon atoms respectively. A biomarker of oxidative damage to lipids caused by smoking, it exists in vivo mainly in the enol form.

concepts.label: reactive nitrogen species
concepts.description: A family of nitrogen molecular entities which are highly reactive and derived from nitric oxide (•NO) and superoxide (O<small><sub>2</sub></small>•<small><sup>−</small></sup>) produced via the enzymatic activity of inducible nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2) and NADPH oxidase respectively.

concepts.label: syringal lignin
concepts.description: Lignin composed principally of trans-sinapyl alcohol (syringyl) units.

concepts.label: lignin
concepts.description: A polyphenylpropanoid derived from three monolignol monomers: trans-p-coumaryl alcohol, coniferol and trans-sinapyl alcohol. There is extensive cross-linking and no defined primary structure.

concepts.label: 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-(1'-sn-glycerol)
concepts.description: A phosphatidylglycerol in which the phosphatidyl moiety has R-configuration and the glycerol moiety has S-configuration.

concepts.label: N-eicosanoylsphinganine
concepts.description: A dihydroceramide in which the ceramide N-acyl group is specified as eicosanoyl

concepts.label: double-stranded RNA
concepts.description: A ribonucleic acid with two complementary strands, similar to the DNA found in all cells.

concepts.label: N-hexadecanoylsphingosine
concepts.description: A N-acylsphingosine in which the ceramide N-acyl group is specified as hexadecanoyl (palmitoyl).

concepts.label: elf18
concepts.description: A polypeptide consisting of the first 18 amino acids at the N-terminus of the Bacterial Elongation Factor Tu protein that is capable of eliciting an innate immunity response in plants.

concepts.label: wax
concepts.description: A chemical substance that is an organic compound or mixture of compounds that is composed of long-chain molecules and is malleable at ambient temperatures.

concepts.label: feruloylagmatine
concepts.description: A member of the class of cinnamamides obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of ferulic acid with the amino group of agmatine.

concepts.label: 1-hexadecyl-2-propionyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine
concepts.description: A 2-acyl-1-alkyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine in which the alkyl and the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are hexadecyl and propionyl respectively.

concepts.label: trypan blue
concepts.description: An organosulfonate salt that is the tetrasodium salt of 3,3'-[(3,3'-dimethylbiphenyl-4,4'-diyl)didiazene-2,1-diyl]bis(5-amino-4-hydroxynaphthalene-2,7-disulfonic acid).

concepts.label: 3,3'-diaminobenzidine
concepts.description: A member of the class of biphenyls that is benzidine in which one of the hydrogens ortho to each of the amino groups has been replaced by an amino group.

concepts.label: Microarray data
concepts.description: Image or hybridisation data for a microarray, typically a study of gene expression.

concepts.label: Nucleic acid melting curve plotting
concepts.description: Calculate and plot a DNA or DNA/RNA melting curve.

concepts.label: Microarrays
concepts.description: Topic concerning microarrays, for example, to process microarray data or design probes and experiments.

concepts.label: Sequencing
concepts.description: Topic concerning the determination of complete (typically nucleotide) sequences, including those of genomes (full genome sequencing, de novo sequencing and resequencing), amplicons and transcriptomes.

concepts.label: Metabolomics
concepts.description: Topic concerning the study of metabolites and the chemical processes they are involved in, especially the systematic study of the chemical fingerprints of specific cellular processes.

concepts.label: mutant
concepts.description: An attribute inhering in a feature bearing a sequence alteration that is present at very low levels in a given population (typically less than 1%), or that has been experimentally generated to alter the feature with respect to some reference sequence.

concepts.label: mutation
concepts.description: A sequence alteration that is very rare allele in a population (typically <1%), or an experimentally-induced variation that derives from a wild-type feature in a given strain.

concepts.label: transiently-expressed transgene
concepts.description: A transgene that is delivered as part of a DNA expression construct into a cell or organism in order to transiently express a specified product (i.e. it has not integrated into the host genome).

concepts.label: wild-type
concepts.description: An allele attribute describing a highly common variant (typically >99% in a population), that typically exhibits canonical function, and against which rare and/or non-functional mutant alleles are compared.

concepts.label: genotype
concepts.description: A specification of the genetic state of an organism, whether complete (defined over the whole genome) or incomplete (defined over a subset of the genome). Genotypes typically describe this genetic state as a diff between some variant component and a canonical reference.

concepts.label: MAPK cascade
concepts.description: An intracellular protein kinase cascade containing at least a MAP kinase (MAPK). It starts with the activation of a MAP3K, and the consecutive activation of a MPK2K and a MAPK. The cascade can also contain an additional tier: the upstream MAP4K. The kinases in each tier phosphorylate and activate the kinase in the downstream tier to transmit a signal within a cell.

concepts.label: innate immune response-activating signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals generated by a ligand binding to its receptor that lead to the activation or perpetuation of an innate immune response.

concepts.label: catalytic activity
concepts.description: Catalysis of a biochemical reaction at physiological temperatures. In biologically catalyzed reactions, the reactants are known as substrates, and the catalysts are naturally occurring macromolecular substances known as enzymes. Enzymes possess specific binding sites for substrates, and are usually composed wholly or largely of protein, but RNA that has catalytic activity (ribozyme) is often also regarded as enzymatic.

concepts.label: GTPase activity
concepts.description: Catalysis of the reaction: GTP + H2O = GDP + H+ + phosphate.

concepts.label: threonine-type endopeptidase activity
concepts.description: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of internal peptide bonds in a polypeptide chain by a mechanism in which the hydroxyl group of a threonine residue at the active center acts as a nucleophile.

concepts.label: cell wall
concepts.description: The rigid or semi-rigid envelope lying outside the cell membrane of plant, fungal, most prokaryotic cells and some protozoan parasites, maintaining their shape and protecting them from osmotic lysis. In plants it is made of cellulose and, often, lignin; in fungi it is composed largely of polysaccharides; in bacteria it is composed of peptidoglycan; in protozoan parasites such as Giardia species, it's made of carbohydrates and proteins.

concepts.label: nucleus
concepts.description: A membrane-bounded organelle of eukaryotic cells in which chromosomes are housed and replicated. In most cells, the nucleus contains all of the cell's chromosomes except the organellar chromosomes, and is the site of RNA synthesis and processing. In some species, or in specialized cell types, RNA metabolism or DNA replication may be absent.

concepts.label: spliceosomal complex
concepts.description: Any of a series of ribonucleoprotein complexes that contain snRNA(s) and small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs), and are formed sequentially during the spliceosomal splicing of one or more substrate RNAs, and which also contain the RNA substrate(s) from the initial target RNAs of splicing, the splicing intermediate RNA(s), to the final RNA products. During cis-splicing, the initial target RNA is a single, contiguous RNA transcript, whether mRNA, snoRNA, etc., and the released products are a spliced RNA and an excised intron, generally as a lariat structure. During trans-splicing, there are two initial substrate RNAs, the spliced leader RNA and a pre-mRNA.

concepts.label: chromosome
concepts.description: A structure composed of a very long molecule of DNA and associated proteins (e.g. histones) that carries hereditary information.

concepts.label: cytoplasm
concepts.description: The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

concepts.label: peroxisome
concepts.description: A small organelle enclosed by a single membrane, and found in most eukaryotic cells. Contains peroxidases and other enzymes involved in a variety of metabolic processes including free radical detoxification, lipid catabolism and biosynthesis, and hydrogen peroxide metabolism.

concepts.label: endoplasmic reticulum
concepts.description: The irregular network of unit membranes, visible only by electron microscopy, that occurs in the cytoplasm of many eukaryotic cells. The membranes form a complex meshwork of tubular channels, which are often expanded into slitlike cavities called cisternae. The ER takes two forms, rough (or granular), with ribosomes adhering to the outer surface, and smooth (with no ribosomes attached).

concepts.label: proteasome core complex
concepts.description: A multisubunit barrel shaped endoprotease complex, which is the core of the proteasome complex.

concepts.label: ribosome
concepts.description: An intracellular organelle, about 200 A in diameter, consisting of RNA and protein. It is the site of protein biosynthesis resulting from translation of messenger RNA (mRNA). It consists of two subunits, one large and one small, each containing only protein and RNA. Both the ribosome and its subunits are characterized by their sedimentation coefficients, expressed in Svedberg units (symbol: S). Hence, the prokaryotic ribosome (70S) comprises a large (50S) subunit and a small (30S) subunit, while the eukaryotic ribosome (80S) comprises a large (60S) subunit and a small (40S) subunit. Two sites on the ribosomal large subunit are involved in translation, namely the aminoacyl site (A site) and peptidyl site (P site). Ribosomes from prokaryotes, eukaryotes, mitochondria, and chloroplasts have characteristically distinct ribosomal proteins.

concepts.label: plasma membrane
concepts.description: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

concepts.label: carbohydrate metabolic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving carbohydrates, any of a group of organic compounds based of the general formula Cx(H2O)y.

concepts.label: generation of precursor metabolites and energy
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of precursor metabolites, substances from which energy is derived, and any process involved in the liberation of energy from these substances.

concepts.label: glycolytic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a carbohydrate into pyruvate, with the concomitant production of a small amount of ATP and the reduction of NAD(P) to NAD(P)H. Glycolysis begins with the metabolism of a carbohydrate to generate products that can enter the pathway and ends with the production of pyruvate. Pyruvate may be converted to acetyl-coenzyme A, ethanol, lactate, or other small molecules.

concepts.label: pentose-phosphate shunt
concepts.description: The metabolic process in which glucose-6-phosphate is oxidized to form carbon dioxide (CO2) and ribulose 5-phosphate, coupled to reduction of NADP+ to NADPH; ribulose 5-P then enters a series of reactions that can yield biosynthetic precursors (ribose-5-phosphate and erythrose-4-phosphate) and glycolytic intermediates (fructose-6-phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate).

concepts.label: nucleosome assembly
concepts.description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a nucleosome, the beadlike structural units of eukaryotic chromatin composed of histones and DNA.

concepts.label: translation
concepts.description: The cellular metabolic process in which a protein is formed, using the sequence of a mature mRNA or circRNA molecule to specify the sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide chain. Translation is mediated by the ribosome, and begins with the formation of a ternary complex between aminoacylated initiator methionine tRNA, GTP, and initiation factor 2, which subsequently associates with the small subunit of the ribosome and an mRNA or circRNA. Translation ends with the release of a polypeptide chain from the ribosome.

concepts.label: protein folding
concepts.description: The process of assisting in the covalent and noncovalent assembly of single chain polypeptides or multisubunit complexes into the correct tertiary structure.

concepts.label: protein phosphorylation
concepts.description: The process of introducing a phosphate group on to a protein.

concepts.label: proteolysis
concepts.description: The hydrolysis of proteins into smaller polypeptides and/or amino acids by cleavage of their peptide bonds.

concepts.label: amino acid metabolic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids, carboxylic acids containing one or more amino groups.

concepts.label: polyamine biosynthetic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of polyamines, any organic compound containing two or more amino groups.

concepts.label: ATP biosynthetic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of ATP, adenosine 5'-triphosphate, a universally important coenzyme and enzyme regulator.

concepts.label: response to stress
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a disturbance in organismal or cellular homeostasis, usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

concepts.label: defense response
concepts.description: Reactions, triggered in response to the presence of a foreign body or the occurrence of an injury, which result in restriction of damage to the organism attacked or prevention/recovery from the infection caused by the attack.

concepts.label: response to osmotic stress
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating an increase or decrease in the concentration of solutes outside the organism or cell.

concepts.label: response to oxidative stress
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of oxidative stress, a state often resulting from exposure to high levels of reactive oxygen species, e.g. superoxide anions, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and hydroxyl radicals.

concepts.label: response to nutrient
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nutrient stimulus.

concepts.label: respiratory gaseous exchange by respiratory system
concepts.description: The process of gaseous exchange between an organism and its environment. In plants, microorganisms, and many small animals, air or water makes direct contact with the organism's cells or tissue fluids, and the processes of diffusion supply the organism with dioxygen (O2) and remove carbon dioxide (CO2). In larger animals the efficiency of gaseous exchange is improved by specialized respiratory organs, such as lungs and gills, which are ventilated by breathing mechanisms.

concepts.label: intracellular protein localization
concepts.description: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

concepts.label: metabolic process
concepts.description: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism transforms chemical substances. This includes including anabolism (biosynthetic process) and catabolism (catabolic process). Metabolic processes includes the transformation of small molecules, as well macromolecular processes such as DNA repair and replication, protein synthesis and degradation.

concepts.label: cell death
concepts.description: Any biological process that results in permanent cessation of all vital functions of a cell. A cell should be considered dead when any one of the following molecular or morphological criteria is met: (1) the cell has lost the integrity of its plasma membrane; (2) the cell, including its nucleus, has undergone complete fragmentation into discrete bodies (frequently referred to as apoptotic bodies). The cell corpse (or its fragments) may be engulfed by an adjacent cell in vivo, but engulfment of whole cells should not be considered a strict criteria to define cell death as, under some circumstances, live engulfed cells can be released from phagosomes (see PMID:18045538).

concepts.label: amino acid biosynthetic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids, organic acids containing one or more amino substituents.

concepts.label: response to heat
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a heat stimulus, a temperature stimulus above the optimal temperature for that organism.

concepts.label: response to water deprivation
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a water deprivation stimulus, prolonged deprivation of water.

concepts.label: thylakoid light-harvesting complex
concepts.description: A thylakoid membrane complex of chlorophylls a and b together with chlorophyll a-b binding proteins. In addition, LHCs contain a number of other proteins, the function of which is speculative, together with accessory pigments. The LHCs capture and transfer energy to photosystems I and II. An example of this is found in Arabidopsis thaliana.

concepts.label: plant-type cell wall
concepts.description: A more or less rigid structure lying outside the cell membrane of a cell and composed of cellulose and pectin and other organic and inorganic substances.

concepts.label: chloroplast
concepts.description: A chlorophyll-containing plastid with thylakoids organized into grana and frets, or stroma thylakoids, and embedded in a stroma.

concepts.label: cytochrome b6f complex
concepts.description: Complex that transfers electrons from reduced plastoquinone to oxidized plastocyanin and translocates protons from the stroma to the lumen. The complex contains a core structure of three catalytic subunits: cytochrome b, the Rieske iron sulfur protein (ISP), and cytochrome f, which are arranged in an integral membrane-bound dimeric complex; additional subunits are present, and vary among different species.

concepts.label: PSI associated light-harvesting complex I
concepts.description: Protein-pigment complex associated with photosystem I.

concepts.label: photosystem
concepts.description: A complex located in a photosynthetic membrane that consists of a photoreaction center associated with accessory pigments and electron carriers. Examples of this component are found in Arabidopsis thaliana and in photosynthetic bacterial and archaeal species.

concepts.label: photosystem II
concepts.description: A photosystem that contains a pheophytin-quinone reaction center with associated accessory pigments and electron carriers. In cyanobacteria and chloroplasts, in the presence of light, PSII functions as a water-plastoquinone oxidoreductase, transferring electrons from water to plastoquinone, whereas other photosynthetic bacteria carry out anoxygenic photosynthesis and oxidize other compounds to re-reduce the photoreaction center.

concepts.label: secondary cell wall
concepts.description: A plant cell wall that is no longer able to expand and so does not permit growth. Secondary cell walls contain less pectin that primary cell walls. The secondary cell is mostly composed of cellulose and is strengthened with lignin.

concepts.label: granum
concepts.description: Distinct stack of lamellae seen within chloroplasts. Grana contain the pigments, electron transfer compounds, and enzymes essential to the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

concepts.label: thylakoid
concepts.description: A membranous cellular structure that bears the photosynthetic pigments in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria. In cyanobacteria thylakoids are of various shapes and are attached to, or continuous with, the plasma membrane. In eukaryotes they are flattened, membrane-bounded disk-like structures located in the chloroplasts; in the chloroplasts of higher plants the thylakoids form dense stacks called grana. Isolated thylakoid preparations can carry out photosynthetic electron transport and the associated phosphorylation.

concepts.label: response to biotic stimulus
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a biotic stimulus, a stimulus caused or produced by a living organism.

concepts.label: plant-type hypersensitive response
concepts.description: The rapid, localized death of plant cells in response to invasion by a pathogen.

concepts.label: response to abiotic stimulus
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an abiotic (not derived from living organisms) stimulus.

concepts.label: photosystem II oxygen evolving complex
concepts.description: A complex, composed of a cluster of manganese, calcium and chloride ions bound to extrinsic proteins, that catalyzes the splitting of water to O2 and 4 H+. In cyanobacteria there are five extrinsic proteins in OEC (PsbO, PsbP-like, PsbQ-like, PsbU and PsbV), while in plants there are only three (PsbO, PsbP and PsbQ).

concepts.label: abscisic acid biosynthetic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of abscisic acid, 5-(1-hydroxy-2,6,6,trimethyl-4-oxocyclohex-2-en-1-y1)-3-methylpenta-2,4-dienoic acid.

concepts.label: phenylpropanoid biosynthetic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of aromatic derivatives of trans-cinnamic acid.

concepts.label: abscisic acid-activated signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals generated by the binding of the plant hormone abscisic acid (ABA) to a receptor, and ending with modulation of a cellular process, e.g. transcription.

concepts.label: hormone-mediated signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of a hormone.

concepts.label: photosynthesis, light harvesting
concepts.description: Absorption and transfer of the energy absorbed from light photons between photosystem reaction centers.

concepts.label: photosynthetic electron transport in photosystem II
concepts.description: A photosynthetic electron transport chain in which electrons move from the primary electron acceptor (Quinone, Q) through a chain of electron transport molecules in the thylakoid membrane until they reach the ultimate electron acceptor of Photosystem II, which is plastocyanin (PC). The electron is then passed to the P700 chlorophyll a molecules of the reaction centre of photosystem I.

concepts.label: cyclic photosynthetic phosphorylation
concepts.description: A photosynthetic phosphorylation process in which ATP synthesis is driven by a proton gradient generated across the thylakoid membrane. Involves only photosystem I.

concepts.label: photosystem II antenna complex
concepts.description: The antenna complex of photosystem II. A photosystem has two closely linked components, an antenna containing light-absorbing pigments and a reaction center. Each antenna contains one or more light-harvesting complexes (LHCs).

concepts.label: embryo development
concepts.description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an embryo from its formation until the end of its embryonic life stage. The end of the embryonic stage is organism-specific. For example, for mammals, the process would begin with zygote formation and end with birth. For insects, the process would begin at zygote formation and end with larval hatching. For plant zygotic embryos, this would be from zygote formation to the end of seed dormancy. For plant vegetative embryos, this would be from the initial determination of the cell or group of cells to form an embryo until the point when the embryo becomes independent of the parent plant.

concepts.label: seed germination
concepts.description: The physiological and developmental changes that occur in a seed commencing with water uptake (imbibition) and terminating with the elongation of the embryonic axis.

concepts.label: photorespiration
concepts.description: A light-dependent catabolic process occurring concomitantly with photosynthesis in plants (especially C3 plants) whereby dioxygen (O2) is consumed and carbon dioxide (CO2) is evolved. The substrate is glycolate formed in large quantities in chloroplasts from 2-phosphoglycolate generated from ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate by the action of ribulose-bisphosphate carboxylase; the glycolate enters the peroxisomes where it is converted by glycolate oxidase to glyoxylate which undergoes transamination to glycine. This then passes into the mitochondria where it is decarboxylated forming one molecule of serine for every two molecules of glycine. This pathway also exists in photosynthetic bacteria.

concepts.label: systemic acquired resistance, salicylic acid mediated signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals mediated by salicylic acid involved in systemic acquired resistance.

concepts.label: salicylic acid mediated signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals mediated by salicylic acid.

concepts.label: jasmonic acid mediated signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals mediated by jasmonic acid.

concepts.label: ethylene-activated signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals generated by the reception of ethylene (ethene, C2H4) by a receptor and ending with modulation of a cellular process, e.g. transcription.

concepts.label: chloroplast fission
concepts.description: The division of a chloroplast within a cell to form two or more separate chloroplast compartments. This division occurs independently of mitosis.

concepts.label: regulation of photosynthesis
concepts.description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of photosynthesis.

concepts.label: transpiration
concepts.description: Release of water by the plant into the air as water vapor mainly through leaves.

concepts.label: leaf senescence
concepts.description: The last stage of leaf development during which programmed degradation of macromolecules and nutrient recycling take place.

concepts.label: nonphotochemical quenching
concepts.description: The process by which excess light energy absorbed by chlorophyll and not used to drive photosynthesis is emitted as heat. This process helps maintain the balance between dissipation and utilization of light energy to minimize generation of oxidizing molecules, thereby protecting the plant against photo-oxidative damage.

concepts.label: photoinhibition
concepts.description: The mechanism by which high light intensity inhibits photosynthesis through inactivation of the D1 protein of photosystem II.

concepts.label: oxygen evolving activity
concepts.description: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 H2O = O2 + 4 H+ + 4 e-. The evolution of oxygen from oxidizing water is carried out by the oxygen evolving complex in photosystem II of plants. P680+, the photochemically oxidized reaction-center chlorophyll of PSII, is a strong biological oxidant. The reduction potential of P680+ is more positive than that of water, and thus it can oxidize water to give O2 and H+ ions. The oxygen escapes as a gas while the H+ ions remain in solution inside the thylakoid vesicle.

concepts.label: heat acclimation
concepts.description: Any process that increases heat tolerance of an organism in response to high temperatures.

concepts.label: gene expression
concepts.description: The process in which a gene's sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA). This includes the production of an RNA transcript and its processing, as well as translation and maturation for protein-coding genes.

concepts.label: programmed cell death
concepts.description: A process which begins when a cell receives an internal or external signal and activates a series of biochemical events (signaling pathway). The process ends with the death of the cell.

concepts.label: protein transport
concepts.description: The directed movement of proteins into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

concepts.label: gas transport
concepts.description: The directed movement of substances that are gaseous in normal living conditions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

concepts.label: carbon fixation
concepts.description: A metabolic process in which carbon (usually derived from carbon dioxide) is incorporated into organic compounds (usually carbohydrates).

concepts.label: photosynthesis
concepts.description: The synthesis by organisms of organic chemical compounds, especially carbohydrates, from carbon dioxide (CO2) using energy obtained from light rather than from the oxidation of chemical compounds.

concepts.label: chlorophyll catabolic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of chlorophyll, any compound of magnesium complexed in a porphyrin (tetrapyrrole) ring and which functions as a photosynthetic pigment, into less complex products.

concepts.label: membrane
concepts.description: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

concepts.label: carotenoid metabolic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving carotenoids, tetraterpenoid compounds in which two units of 4 isoprenoid residues joined head-to-tail are themselves joined tail-to-tail.

concepts.label: antioxidant activity
concepts.description: Inhibition of the reactions brought about by dioxygen (O2) or peroxides. Usually the antioxidant is effective because it can itself be more easily oxidized than the substance protected. The term is often applied to components that can trap free radicals, thereby breaking the chain reaction that normally leads to extensive biological damage.

concepts.label: protein oxidation
concepts.description: The modification of a protein amino acid by oxidation.

concepts.label: virion attachment to host cell
concepts.description: The process by which a virion protein binds to molecules on the host cellular surface or host cell surface projection.

concepts.label: viral genome replication
concepts.description: Any process involved directly in viral genome replication, including viral nucleotide metabolism.

concepts.label: reductive pentose-phosphate cycle
concepts.description: The fixation of carbon dioxide (CO2) as glucose in the chloroplasts of C3 plants; uses ATP and NADPH formed in the light reactions of photosynthesis; carbon dioxide reacts with ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate (catalyzed by the function of ribulose-bisphosphate carboxylase) to yield two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate; these are then phosphorylated by ATP to 1,3-bisphosphateglyceraldehyde which, in turn, is then reduced by NADPH to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. The glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate is converted to fructose 5-phosphate and ribulose 5-phosphate by aldolase and other enzymes; the ribulose 5-phosphate is phosphorylated by ATP to ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate.

concepts.label: ammonia oxidation
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways by which ammonia or ammonium is converted to molecular nitrogen or another nitrogen compound, with accompanying loss of electrons.

concepts.label: aerobic respiration, using ammonia as electron donor
concepts.description: The metabolic process in which ammonia (NH4+) is oxidized to nitrite (NO2) in the presence of oxygen; enzymatic reactions convert ammonia to hydrazine, and hydrazine to nitrite.

concepts.label: calcium-mediated signaling
concepts.description: Any intracellular signal transduction in which the signal is passed on within the cell via calcium ions.

concepts.label: nitrogen utilization
concepts.description: A series of processes that forms an integrated mechanism by which a cell or an organism detects the depletion of primary nitrogen source, usually ammonia, and then activates genes to scavenge the last traces of the primary nitrogen source and to transport and metabolize alternative nitrogen sources. The utilization process begins when the cell or organism detects nitrogen levels, includes the activation of genes whose products detect, transport or metabolize nitrogen-containing substances, and ends when nitrogen is incorporated into the cell or organism's metabolism.

concepts.label: electron transport chain
concepts.description: A process in which a series of electron carriers operate together to transfer electrons from donors to any of several different terminal electron acceptors.

concepts.label: signaling
concepts.description: The entirety of a process in which information is transmitted within a biological system. This process begins with an active signal and ends when a cellular response has been triggered.

concepts.label: type III protein secretion system complex
concepts.description: A complex of approximately 20 proteins, most of which are located in the cytoplasmic membrane that carries out protein secretion in the bacterial type III secretion system; type III secretion also requires a cytoplasmic, probably membrane-associated ATPase.

concepts.label: endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of the presence of unfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) or other ER-related stress; results in changes in the regulation of transcription and translation.

concepts.label: regulatory ncRNA-mediated gene silencing
concepts.description: A process in which an regulatory non-coding RNA molecule reduces expression of target genes. This can occur pre-transcriptionally by assembly of heterochromatin and prevention of transcription or co- or post-transcriptionally by targeting RNAs for degradation or by interfering with splicing or translation. This process starts once the inhibitory RNA molecule has been transcribed, and includes processing of the RNA such as cleavage, modifications, transport from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, loading onto the RISC complex, and the effect on transcription or translation.

concepts.label: chloroplast membrane
concepts.description: Either of the lipid bilayers that surround a chloroplast and form the chloroplast envelope.

concepts.label: photosynthetic membrane
concepts.description: A membrane enriched in complexes formed of reaction centers, accessory pigments and electron carriers, in which photosynthetic reactions take place.

concepts.label: lipid oxidation
concepts.description: The removal of one or more electrons from a lipid, with or without the concomitant removal of a proton or protons, by reaction with an electron-accepting substance, by addition of oxygen or by removal of hydrogen.

concepts.label: arbuscular mycorrhizal association
concepts.description: A form of mutualism between a fungus and the roots of a vascular plant, where hyphae of the fungus penetrate the plant cell wall and invaginate its cell membrane. Once inside, the fungus forms highly branched structures for nutrient exchange with the plant called arbuscules. Aids in the acquisition by the plant of nutrients such as phosphorus from the soil.

concepts.label: growth
concepts.description: The increase in size or mass of an entire organism, a part of an organism or a cell.

concepts.label: nitrate assimilation
concepts.description: The nitrogen metabolic process that encompasses the uptake of nitrate from the environment and reduction to ammonia, and results in the incorporation of nitrogen derived from nitrate into cellular substances.

concepts.label: thylakoid membrane
concepts.description: The pigmented membrane of any thylakoid.

concepts.label: post-translational protein modification
concepts.description: The process of covalently altering one or more amino acids in a protein after the protein has been completely translated and released from the ribosome.

concepts.label: protein folding chaperone
concepts.description: Binding to a protein or a protein-containing complex to assist the protein folding process.

concepts.label: biological process involved in symbiotic interaction
concepts.description: A process carried out by gene products in an organism that enable the organism to engage in a symbiotic relationship, a more or less intimate association, with another organism. The various forms of symbiosis include parasitism, in which the association is disadvantageous or destructive to one of the organisms; mutualism, in which the association is advantageous, or often necessary to one or both and not harmful to either; and commensalism, in which one member of the association benefits while the other is not affected. However, mutualism, parasitism, and commensalism are often not discrete categories of interactions and should rather be perceived as a continuum of interaction ranging from parasitism to mutualism. In fact, the direction of a symbiotic interaction can change during the lifetime of the symbionts due to developmental changes as well as changes in the biotic/abiotic environment in which the interaction occurs. Microscopic symbionts are often referred to as endosymbionts.

concepts.label: innate immune response
concepts.description: Innate immune responses are defense responses mediated by germline encoded components that directly recognize components of potential pathogens.

concepts.label: cellular respiration
concepts.description: The enzymatic release of energy from inorganic and organic compounds (especially carbohydrates and fats) which either requires oxygen (aerobic respiration) or does not (anaerobic respiration).

concepts.label: cell redox homeostasis
concepts.description: Any process that maintains the redox environment of a cell or compartment within a cell.

concepts.label: respiratory burst
concepts.description: A phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

concepts.label: negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription
concepts.description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cellular DNA-templated transcription.

concepts.label: glycolate catabolic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of glycolate, the anion of hydroxyethanoic acid (glycolic acid).

concepts.label: transport of virus
concepts.description: The directed movement of a virus, or part of a virus, into, out of, or within a host cell.

concepts.label: ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase activator activity
concepts.description: Binds to and iincreases the activity of rubisco by the removal of otherwise inhibitory sugar phosphates: RuBP, and in some plants, 2-carboxyarabinitol 1-phosphate.

concepts.label: apoplast
concepts.description: The cell membranes and intracellular regions in a plant are connected through plasmodesmata, and plants may be described as having two major compartments: the living symplast and the non-living apoplast. The apoplast is external to the plasma membrane and includes cell walls, intercellular spaces and the lumen of dead structures such as xylem vessels. Water and solutes pass freely through it.

concepts.label: lignin network
concepts.description: An extracellular matrix part that consists of lignin in the form of a three-dimensional polymeric network. Lignins are complex racemic aromatic heteropolymers derived from a variety of phenylpropane monomers coupled together by an assortment of carbon-carbon and ether linkages. Lignin is crucial for structural integrity of the cell wall and stiffness and strength of the stem. In addition, lignin waterproofs the cell wall, enabling transport of water and solutes through the vascular system, and plays a role in protecting plants against pathogens.

concepts.label: flower formation
concepts.description: The process that gives rise to the flower. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts.

concepts.label: L-gulonolactone oxidase activity
concepts.description: Catalysis of the reaction: L-gulono-1,4-lactone + O2 = L-xylo-hex-3-ulonolactone + H2O2.

concepts.label: protein stabilization
concepts.description: Any process involved in maintaining the structure and integrity of a protein and preventing it from degradation or aggregation.

concepts.label: response to stimulus
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus. The process begins with detection of the stimulus and ends with a change in state or activity or the cell or organism.

concepts.label: cellular response to stimulus
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus. The process begins with detection of the stimulus by a cell and ends with a change in state or activity or the cell.

concepts.label: cell wall thickening
concepts.description: A type of cell wall modification in which the cell wall is reinforced and made thicker.

concepts.label: cellular response to osmotic stress
concepts.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating an increase or decrease in the concentration of solutes outside the organism or cell.

concepts.label: nitrogen cycle metabolic process
concepts.description: A nitrogen compound metabolic process that contributes to the nitrogen cycle. The nitrogen cycle is a series of metabolic pathways by which nitrogen is converted between various forms and redox states; it encompasses pathways in which nitrogen is acted upon directly, such as nitrification, denitrification, nitrogen fixation, and mineralization.

concepts.label: effector-mediated activation of plant hypersensitive response by symbiont
concepts.description: A symbiont process in which a molecule secreted by the symbiont activates a resistance gene-dependent defense response signaling pathway in the plant host, in order to activate a hypersensitive response to induce necrosis. In the plant, this process involves the direct or indirect recognition of the symbiont effector protein for example through plant resistance receptor or R proteins (or R genes).

concepts.label: developmental vegetative growth
concepts.description: The increase in size or mass of non-reproductive plant parts.

concepts.label: stomatal closure
concepts.description: The process of closing of stomata, pores in the epidermis of leaves and stems bordered by two guard cells and serving in gas exchange.

concepts.label: chlorophyll fluorescence
concepts.description: The process by which excess light energy absorbed by chlorophyll and not used to drive photosynthesis is re-emitted as light.

concepts.label: programmed necrotic cell death
concepts.description: A necrotic cell death process that results from the activation of endogenous cellular processes, such as signaling involving death domain receptors or Toll-like receptors.

concepts.label: import across plasma membrane
concepts.description: The directed movement of some substance from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

concepts.label: cellular oxidant detoxification
concepts.description: Any process carried out at the cellular level that reduces or removes the toxicity superoxide radicals or hydrogen peroxide.

concepts.label: ammonium import across plasma membrane
concepts.description: The directed movement of an ammonium ion from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

concepts.label: pathogen-associated molecular pattern receptor signaling pathway
concepts.description: The series of molecular signals initiated by a ligand binding of a pattern recognition receptor (PRR) to activate a plant innate immune response. PAMP-triggered immunity PRRs bind pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMPs), structures conserved among microbial species.

concepts.label: nitrate import
concepts.description: The directed movement of nitrate into a cell or organelle.

concepts.label: reactive oxygen species biosynthetic process
concepts.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of reactive oxygen species, any molecules or ions formed by the incomplete one-electron reduction of oxygen.

concepts.label: negative regulation of photosynthesis
concepts.description: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of photosynthesis.

concepts.label: organomineral extracellular matrix
concepts.description: An extracellular matrix consisting of a densely packed organomineral assembly in which the mineral phase represents the majority of the material by weight.
